blocks.text: 3 Methodology

We formalize a short segment of training as a multi-time stochastic process that maps instruments —controllable, randomized interventions—to a distribution over observables on a fixed probe set. The key object is a classical process tensor (comb) acting at two times; our operational witness of memory is a back-flow of distinguishability between two one-step histories under a fixed second intervention. We prove that a positive back-flow contradicts an operational Markov condition at the observable, and we show that a causal break (resetting optimizer buffers) restores that condition under a mild sufficiency hypothesis, predicting the collapse of our witness.

3.2 Operational Markov condition at the observable

Operational Markov condition (OMC) at the observable . Fix a second-step instrument B B . We say that the two-time process is operationally Markov at the observable for B B if there exists a stochastic map Λ B : 𝒫 ⁡ ( 𝒪 ) → 𝒫 ⁡ ( 𝒪 ) \Lambda_{B}:\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{O})\to\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{O}) such that for every first-step instrument I I ,

If the two-time process is operationally Markov at the observable for B B , then for any contractive divergence D D , the back-flow of distinguishability satisfies Δ ( I , B ) ≤ 0 \Delta^{(I,B)}\leq 0 for all I I .

Intuitively, once the observed mid-time law Φ 1 \Phi_{1} is fixed, B B acts by the same channel on it, independent of how Φ 1 \Phi_{1} was prepared. Condition ( 4 ) is strictly weaker than assuming latent Markov dynamics in ( θ , buffers ) (\theta,\text{buffers}) : it only constrains the measured map.
3.3 A back-flow witness of operational memory

Choose two first-step instruments A , A ′ A,A^{\prime} (same indices, different augmentation) and fix B B . Let D D be a divergence on 𝒫 ⁡ ( 𝒪 ) \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{O}) that obeys data processing (see § 3.6 ). Define
Δ BF := D 2 − D 1 . \Delta_{\!\mathrm{BF}}:=D_{2}-D_{1}. (7)
If ( 4 ) holds and D D satisfies data processing, then Δ BF ≤ 0 \Delta_{\!\mathrm{BF}}\leq 0 .

Thus, positive back-flow ( Δ BF > 0 \Delta_{\!\mathrm{BF}}>0 ) falsifies ( 4 ) and witnesses operational memory at the two-step scale. Mechanistically this can arise because (i) history is carried across the step by unobserved buffers that modulate the action of B B , or (ii) the observable is insufficient for how B B acts: two distinct latent preparations that agree on Φ 1 \Phi_{1} evolve differently under B B .
3.4 Causal break and a sufficient condition for restoring OMC

A causal break before B B is a kernel ℬ : 𝒮 ↝ 𝒮 \mathcal{B}:\mathcal{S}\leadsto\mathcal{S} that erases a memory channel we intend to cut. In our setting, it resets optimizer buffers while keeping parameters fixed: if s = ( θ , υ ) s=(\theta,\upsilon) , then ℬ ⁡ ( s , d ​ θ ′ ​ d ​ υ ′ ) = δ θ ​ ( d ​ θ ′ ) ​ δ 0 ​ ( d ​ υ ′ ) \mathcal{B}(s,\mathrm{d}\theta^{\prime}\mathrm{d}\upsilon^{\prime})=\delta_{\theta}(\mathrm{d}\theta^{\prime})\,\delta_{0}(\mathrm{d}\upsilon^{\prime}) . Let 𝒦 ~ B := 𝒦 B ⋆ ℬ \widetilde{\mathcal{K}}_{B}:=\mathcal{K}_{B}\star\mathcal{B} be the post-break latent kernel.
We give a mild, checkable condition under which the break implies ( 4 ).

Let 𝒬 ⊆ 𝒫 ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) \mathcal{Q}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{S}) be the set of mid-time latent laws reachable after the first step. The observation channel 𝒪 \mathcal{O} is sufficient for B B on 𝒬 \mathcal{Q} if for any π 1 , π 1 ′ ∈ 𝒬 \pi_{1},\pi_{1}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Q} with equal observables π 1 ​ 𝒪 − 1 = π 1 ′ ​ 𝒪 − 1 \pi_{1}\mathcal{O}^{-1}=\pi_{1}^{\prime}\mathcal{O}^{-1} , we also have π 1 ​ 𝒦 ~ B ​ 𝒪 − 1 = π 1 ′ ​ 𝒦 ~ B ​ 𝒪 − 1 \pi_{1}\widetilde{\mathcal{K}}_{B}\mathcal{O}^{-1}=\pi_{1}^{\prime}\widetilde{\mathcal{K}}_{B}\mathcal{O}^{-1} .

(Break ⇒ \Rightarrow observable channel under sufficiency.) If a causal break ℬ \mathcal{B} is applied and 𝒪 \mathcal{O} is sufficient for B B on 𝒬 \mathcal{Q} , then there exists a stochastic map Λ B \Lambda_{B} on 𝒫 ⁡ ( 𝒪 ) \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{O}) such that for all first-step instruments I I , Φ 2 ( I , B ) = Λ B ​ [ Φ 1 ( I ) ] \Phi_{2}^{(I,B)}=\Lambda_{B}[\Phi_{1}^{(I)}] . Consequently, Δ BF ≤ 0 \Delta_{\!\mathrm{BF}}\leq 0 for any contractive divergence D D .

A sufficient way to ensure Def. 2 is a Markov factorization through the observable: there exists a lifting kernel R : 𝒪 ↝ 𝒮 R:\mathcal{O}\leadsto\mathcal{S} (a right-inverse of 𝒪 \mathcal{O} on 𝒬 \mathcal{Q} ) such that 𝒦 ~ B = 𝒦 ~ B ⋆ R ⋆ 𝒪 \widetilde{\mathcal{K}}_{B}=\widetilde{\mathcal{K}}_{B}\star R\star\mathcal{O} on 𝒬 \mathcal{Q} . Then Λ B = 𝒪 ⋆ 𝒦 ~ B ⋆ R \Lambda_{B}=\mathcal{O}\star\widetilde{\mathcal{K}}_{B}\star R is explicit.

3.6 Divergences and contractivity

We operate on per-example predictive distributions over the probe set and aggregate by averaging the per-example divergence. 1 1 1 Formally, if x ∈ 𝒫 x\in\mathcal{P} ranges over probe inputs and P x , Q x P_{x},Q_{x} are the class-probability vectors under two histories, we use D ¯ ​ ( P , Q ) := 1 | 𝒫 | ​ ∑ x ∈ 𝒫 D ⁡ ( P x , Q x ) \bar{D}(P,Q):=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{P}|}\sum_{x\in\mathcal{P}}D(P_{x},Q_{x}) . If D D obeys data processing pointwise, so does D ¯ \bar{D} . We require boundedness in [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] , sensitivity to multi-class changes, and data processing: total variation TV ⁡ ( p , q ) = 1 2 ​ ‖ p − q ‖ 1 , \mathrm{TV}(p,q)=\tfrac{1}{2}\|p-q\|_{1}, and Hellinger Hell ⁡ ( p , q ) = 1 2 ​ ‖ p − q ‖ 2 \mathrm{Hell}(p,q)=\tfrac{1}{2}\left\|\sqrt{p}-\sqrt{q}\right\|_{2} are f f -divergences and thus contractive under stochastic maps; Jensen–Shannon JS ( p , q ) = 1 2 KL ( p ∥ m ) + 1 2 KL ( q ∥ m ) , m = 1 2 ( p + q ) \mathrm{JS}(p,q)=\tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{KL}(p\|m)+\tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{KL}(q\|m),~m=\tfrac{1}{2}(p+q) is a symmetrized mixture of KL \operatorname{KL} and inherits the same property. Proposition 3.2 therefore applies to all three.
3.7 Inference at the observable level

Each run produces random variables D 1 , D 2 ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] D_{1},D_{2}\in[0,1] and Δ BF ∈ [ − 1 , 1 ] \Delta_{\!\mathrm{BF}}\in[-1,1] . We treat the operational Markov inequality as the null H 0 : 𝔼 ⁡ [ Δ BF ] ≤ 0 H_{0}:\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{\!\mathrm{BF}}]\leq 0 . We report nonparametric bootstrap CIs for the mean and perform TOST ( two one-sided tests ) against a small equivalence margin ε \varepsilon to declare practical nullity. A lower confidence bound strictly above 0 0 rejects H 0 H_{0} and certifies operational non-Markovianity for the specified instruments and observable; collapse toward 0 0 after a causal break supports the mechanism diagnosis in § 3.4 .
3.8 What a positive back-flow means (and what it does not)

A strictly positive Δ BF \Delta_{\!\mathrm{BF}} says there is no single channel Λ B \Lambda_{B} that maps the measured one-step laws to the two-step laws for the fixed B B . It does not claim the augmented latent dynamics ( θ , buffers ) (\theta,\text{buffers}) are non-Markov; rather, it pinpoints an observable-level failure of ( 4 ). Our causal-break experiments remove optimizer memory as a carrier and are consistent with the picture that, at the two-step scale we probe, buffers mediate the observed dependence.

4.1 Micro-step protocol ( A A then B B )

A single micro-experiment starts from the cached base parameters, applies k k SGD steps on a mini-batch stream from A A , then k k steps from B B . Unless otherwise specified: batch size 256 256 , per-step weight decay 10 − 4 10^{-4} , gradient clip at 1.0 1.0 , channels-last memory layout, and AMP disabled (the code path supports it but we keep it off in the sweep). BatchNorm running statistics are frozen during micro-steps.

We implement GPU-native transforms: weak = random crop ( 32 32 , reflect pad 4 4 ) + horizontal flip ( p = 0.5 p{=}0.5 ); color = weak + color jitter (brightness/contrast/saturation 0.4 0.4 ) + random grayscale ( p = 0.2 p{=}0.2 ); blur = weak + depthwise Gaussian blur (kernel 3 3 , σ ∼ 𝒰 ⁡ [ 0.1 , 2.0 ] \sigma\!\sim\!\mathcal{U}[0.1,2.0] ); and none = identity.

For each repeat we draw I A I_{A} uniformly without replacement (size 256 256 ) from cached training tensors. We draw I B I_{B} to achieve a prescribed overlap with I A I_{A} , | I A ∩ I B | ≈ ⌊ overlap × 256 ⌋ |I_{A}\cap I_{B}|\approx\lfloor\texttt{overlap}\times 256\rfloor , and optionally match the class histogram of I A I_{A} ( same_classes=True ), otherwise draw from the complement. This gives fine control of content resonance between A A and B B .

4.3 Repeats, seeds, precision targets

For each (dataset, model, regime, break flag) and each seed s ∈ { 0 , 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 } s\in\{0,1,2,3,4\} , we run R = 128 R{=}128 independent repeats (fresh ( I A , I B ) (I_{A},I_{B}) per repeat). To control runtime while keeping tight confidence intervals, after at least 64 64 repeats we check every 32 32 repeats whether the nominal half-width of the 95% CI for Δ BF ¯ \overline{\Delta_{\!\mathrm{BF}}} (normal approximation) is ≤ 2 × 10 − 4 \leq 2{\times}10^{-4} and stop early if so. We then aggregate per-configuration means with 2000-sample nonparametric bootstrap CIs (on per-repeat Δ BF \Delta_{\!\mathrm{BF}} ). For completeness we also perform TOST with equivalence margin ε = 10 − 3 \varepsilon{=}10^{-3} . All micro-experiments use SGD; gradients are clipped at 1.0 1.0 ; a NaN guard and a fallback LR scaling ( × 0.5 \times 0.5 on retry) handle rare numerical issues. We freeze BN running stats during micro-steps, and run inference in channels-last format. The orchestration writes per-seed logs and a post-processing script emits a summary with mean Δ BF \Delta_{\!\mathrm{BF}} and bootstrap CIs, alongside diagnostic figures 2 2 2 These artifacts are the basis for § 5 .

For the setups in Fig. 4 , the non-commute curve TV ( A ​ B , B ​ A ) (AB,BA) increases with the number of micro-steps k k , evidencing order sensitivity even at short horizons. Regarding the limitations of this work we restrict to short two-step interventions, image classification benchmarks, and standard vision backbones; we study the existence and controllability of memory rather than downstream benefits. Our diagnostic complements, not replaces, SDE/Markov analyses, and it inherits the usual caveats of probe design (choice of B B , probe set, metric).
